content.title: About
content.content: The egg white sandwich with cheese consists of whole‑grain bread, tender egg white, melted cheese, and often includes lettuce or vegetables. It is a light yet nourishing breakfast or snack option, rich in protein and calcium.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white is almost pure protein and contains virtually no fat.
Cheese adds flavor as well as calcium and vitamin D.
Whole‑grain bread contributes dietary fiber that supports digestion.
This sandwich is frequently offered in fast‑casual cafés as a "low‑calorie" breakfast choice.
The protein‑carb combination helps maintain steady energy levels for several hours.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A typical serving provides about 10 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Unlike whole eggs, egg white contains virtually no fat, making the sandwich suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese contributes a notable amount of calcium, essential for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Fiber from whole‑grain bread
items.content: Fiber improves digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The combination of egg white and whole‑grain bread supplies B2, B6, and folate, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to egg white, experiencing skin reactions or more severe symptoms.

items.title: Lactose in cheese
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort from the cheese used in the sandwich.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain processed cheeses contain added salt, which should be considered for low‑sodium diets.

items.title: Gluten in bread
items.content: Whole‑grain bread contains gluten, making the product unsuitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich warm, lightly toasting the bread until golden. Add fresh vegetables such as tomato, cucumber, or spinach to boost vitamin and mineral intake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sandwich in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours. Keep the bread and filling separate to prevent sogginess. Reheat in a toaster or microwave if desired.
